observations: All six fixed-camera rear screenshots were personally inspected at their original 1280 by 800 resolution. Both motorcycles show the tapered carbon arm, machined axle end, visible chain run and dark undertail. The damper remains attached in the static and loaded captures; no floating rear part or new visible boot/arm obstruction was found in these views.

All four right-peg dry/wet closeups were inspected. The sole and peg remain together while the revised carbon neck runs inboard and below the boot. Screenshot observation supports the numerical sampled-volume regression but does not quantify three-dimensional clearance.

All four dry/wet corner images were inspected. Rider lean/hang-off and the braking pose change are visible, with the rider remaining assembled and attached to the motorcycle. These wide overhead images are useful pose evidence but do not expose rear hardware as clearly as the rear/peg cameras.

Both high-detail front images and the GP-R1 recovery image were inspected. The visible GP-R1 exhaust shell, retained carbon strap, vanes and their shading have no visible batching discontinuity. Recovery is a deliberate separate standing pose, not a rear-clearance measurement.
Loaded dry and loaded wet rear captures use the same camera and pose. Wet captures visibly change tyre and painted-surface highlights while preserving the mechanical arrangement.

The render remains a procedural game model, with visibly simplified rider armour and body surfaces. This evidence establishes the implemented mechanical refinement and repeatability rather than equivalence to a reference photograph.

limits: ANGLE/Mesa llvmpipe software WebGL2 rendering; physical hardware and game FPS are not established by this evidence.
The final rear static/loaded/wet images compare states of the same final model. They are not a before/after of the original reference-driven geometry implementation.
The four byte-identical PNG comparisons isolate preservation relative to the earlier 9d5 implementation; they do not imply every possible camera and pose has identical pixels.
Rear calls include the fixture renderer passes; expanded asset triangle counts differ from submitted multi-pass triangles.
Render hashes establish the prescribed repeated-state relationships within each test, not universal cross-platform hash identity.
Numerical boot clearance is sampled, and the separate source-level contract includes a finer 4 mm sweep plus actual-arm three-dimensional chain clearance checks.
Local SwiftShader attempt was interrupted after exact-runtime Mesa passes and yielded no completed local case; retain its exit 130 and incomplete scope.
